title: beyou-server · Overview
description: The host and the k3s node at a glance: how busy it is, how it behaves over time, and which namespaces and pods use what.

panels.title: CPU in use
panels.description: Share of all cores busy (user + system + irq), averaged over the rate window. I/O wait is shown apart.

panels.title: Memory in use
panels.description: Total RAM minus what the kernel says is available (free + reclaimable cache).

panels.title: Memory available
panels.description: Room left before the kernel starts swapping hard or OOM-killing.

panels.title: Swap in use
panels.description: Pages pushed out of RAM. Some is normal; a growing number is the warning sign.

panels.title: Load / cores
panels.description: 1-minute load divided by the cores. Above 100% means work is queueing (CPU or disk).

panels.title: CPU temperature
panels.description: Hottest core.

panels.title: Root disk
panels.description: Used space on / (the SSD: k3s, images, volumes).

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Since the last reboot of the host.

panels.title: Pods running
panels.description: Pods in phase Running on the node.

panels.title: Pods not ready
panels.description: Running pods whose readiness probe is failing.

panels.title: Restarts (24 h)
panels.description: Container restarts across the cluster in the last day.

panels.title: OOM kills (24 h)
panels.description: Containers killed by the kernel for going over their memory limit.

panels.title: Memory requested
panels.description: Sum of memory requests of running pods over what the node offers. Near 100% new pods stop scheduling.

panels.title: Memory limits
panels.description: Sum of memory limits over the node. Above 100% is overcommit: fine while pods stay below their limits.

panels.title: Memory pressure
panels.description: Share of time some task was stalled waiting for memory (PSI). Above a few % the node is thrashing.

panels.title: I/O pressure
panels.description: Share of time some task was stalled waiting for disk (PSI). Swap storms show up here.

panels.title: CPU by mode
panels.description: Share of all cores, stacked: the top of the stack is total CPU in use. iowait is time idle waiting for disk.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: RAM stacked to its total: used (not reclaimable), cache the kernel can give back, and free. Available = cache + free.

panels.title: Swap and paging
panels.description: How much has been pushed out of RAM. See the pressure panel for whether it is hurting.

panels.title: Pressure (time stalled)
panels.description: Linux PSI: the share of time at least one task was waiting on CPU, memory or disk. The clearest 'is the node struggling' signal.

panels.title: Load vs cores
panels.description: Runnable plus disk-blocked tasks. Above the cores line, work is waiting.

panels.title: CPU temperature
panels.description: Hottest core over time.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Reads above the line, writes below. sda is the system SSD, sdb the photo HDD.

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Share of time each disk had I/O in flight. Near 100% the disk is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Physical NICs and Tailscale. In above the line, out below.

panels.title: Memory by namespace
panels.description: Working set per namespace, stacked; the top of the stack is the node's memory in use. 'k3s itself' is the k3s process (API server, kubelet, containerd); 'rest of the host' is the kernel and everything run outside Kubernetes (Tailscale, cloudflared, shells).

panels.title: CPU by namespace
panels.description: Cores used per namespace, stacked; the top is the node's busy CPU. 'k3s itself' is the API server, kubelet and containerd; 'rest of the host' is everything outside Kubernetes.

panels.title: Memory now, by namespace
panels.description: Working set right now, with k3s and the rest of the host as their own bars.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by(namespace)(container_memory_working_set_bytes{container!=""}) or label_replace(sum(container_memory_working_set_bytes{id="/system.slice/k3s.service"}), "namespace", "k3s itself", "", "") or label_replace(clamp_min(sum(node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{job="node-exporter"} - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{job="node-exporter"}) - sum(container_memory_working_set_bytes{container!=""}) - sum(container_memory_working_set_bytes{id="/system.slice/k3s.service"}), 0), "namespace", "rest of the host", "", ""))

panels.title: CPU now, by namespace
panels.description: Average over the last 5 minutes, with k3s as its own bar.

panels.title: Memory used vs quota
panels.description: Each namespace's ResourceQuota: sum of memory limits declared vs the cap. Full means new pods there will be refused.

panels.title: Memory used vs requested
panels.description: Working set over memory requests. Well above 100%: the namespace uses more than the scheduler reserved for it, which is how the node ends up swapping.

panels.title: Memory by pod (top 15)
panels.description: Working set of the 15 biggest pods in the selected namespaces.

panels.title: CPU by pod (top 15)
panels.description: Cores used by the 15 busiest pods in the selected namespaces.

panels.title: Containers: usage vs requests and limits
panels.description: One row per running container. Memory % of limit near 100% means an OOM kill is close; Throttled is the share of CPU periods the container was capped by its CPU limit.

panels.title: Restarts by namespace
panels.description: Container restarts per hour. Bursts across many namespaces at once usually mean the node itself stalled (swap or I/O), not the apps.

panels.title: OOM kills
panels.description: Kills by the kernel for memory, per hour.

panels.title: CPU throttling (top 10)
panels.description: Share of CPU periods a pod was capped by its CPU limit. High values mean slow responses even with idle cores.
